t: That, effective on the first day of the month following enactment of this bill, the first section and section 2 of the Act entitled “An Act to provide benefits for widows of certain persons who were retired or are eligible for retirement under section 6 of the Act entitled ‘An Act to authorize aids to navigation and for other works in the Lighthouse Service, and for other purposes’, approved June 20, 1918, as amended”, approved August 19, 1950 (33 U.S.C. 771 and 772), are each amended by striking out “$75 per month” and inserting in lieu thereof “$100 per month”.

fable.w: This section only raises the monthly benefit for widows of Lighthouse Service retirees from $75 to $100. The one tempting reading is that it concerns benefits for members of the public, but receiving a benefit is not participating in a federal decision. Nothing in the text provides for consultation, hearings, comment, rulemaking, an advisory body, or a right to sue.
fable.s: are each amended by striking out “$75 per month” and inserting in lieu thereof “$100 per month”

qwen_block.w: This section amends a statute to change the monetary amount of a benefit for widows. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in the decision-making process. It is a substantive change to benefit levels, not a procedural requirement for public input.
qwen_block.s: striking out “$75 per month” and inserting in lieu thereof “$100 per month”

opus.w: This section only raises the monthly benefit for widows of certain Lighthouse Service retirees from $75 to $100. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue that would bring outside parties into a federal decision. The mention of benefits might suggest participation, but benefits are expressly excluded, and here there isn't even an application process.
opus.s: are each amended by striking out “$75 per month” and inserting in lieu thereof “$100 per month”
opus.b: **Step 1 — Analysis.** The section mentions "benefits for widows" and "retirement," so one might file it under applications for benefits. That reading still doesn't make it participation, because the definition excludes benefits. More importantly, the section only raises a widows' benefit from $75 to $100 per month. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. No one outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the statutory amount of a benefit for widows. The definition explicitly states that participation 'does not include applications for benefits or grants.' Furthermore, there is no requirement for consultation, public comment, or coordination with outside entities before this change is enacted; it is a direct legislative amendment. Therefore, it does not involve participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: are each amended by striking out “$75 per month” and inserting in lieu thereof “$100 per month”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing benefit amounts affects the public, but the definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants." This section merely sets the statutory amount of a benefit; it does not create a process for public consultation, comment, or participation in the decision-making process. The decision is made by Congress via amendment, not through interaction with outside parties.
